report.summary: All three failures are the same Page.goto('/books') timeout at 5 s, and none reached an assertion. The app's list_books() adds a random 0–8 s sleep on every /books render, so roughly 3 in 8 page loads exceed the 5 s budget; this is flakiness, not a deterministic product bug. First step: remove or bound that artificial delay in app/main.py:150 (or, if it is intentional, make the tests wait for it explicitly), then rerun the UI suite a few times to confirm.

causes.title: Random 0–8 s server delay on /books exceeds the 5 s navigation timeout
causes.explanation: list_books() calls time.sleep(random.uniform(0, 8)) before querying the database (app/main.py:149-150). render_books() calls list_books() on every render of the books page (app/main.py:256), so every GET /books waits a random 0–8 s. The UI fixture sets page.set_default_timeout(5000) (tests/ui/conftest.py:7), and Page.goto waits for the 'load' event, so any response slower than 5 s raises TimeoutError. The chance of a sleep over 5 s is about 3/8, which matches the three failures and the one passing test that also opens /books (test_deleted_book_disappears). The same code can pass on a rerun, so this is flaky. The root cause sits in the app (an artificial, variable delay), and the tests are right to expect a prompt page.
evidence: app/main.py:256: "books": list_books(user["id"]),  (called from render_books on every /books render)
tests/ui/conftest.py:6-7: "Nothing in this app should take longer than 5 s" ... page.set_default_timeout(5000)
Failure text for all three: playwright._impl._errors.TimeoutError: Page.goto: Timeout 5000ms exceeded. Call log: navigating to "http://127.0.0.1:49185/books", waiting until "load"
tests/ui/test_books_ui.py:31: test_deleted_book_disappears also opens /books via BooksPage.open() and is not in the failure list, consistent with a random delay
The failures occur before any assertion (tests/ui/test_books_ui.py:10, 23, 39), so no evidence points to a locator or assertion problem in the tests
causes.suggested_fix: Remove the time.sleep(random.uniform(0, 8)) from list_books() in app/main.py, since it has no purpose in production code. If the delay is deliberately simulating slowness, do not put it on the shared render path; instead, have the tests tolerate it: give BooksPage.open() a longer goto timeout (for example page.goto('/books', timeout=15000)) or wait for a specific element. Then rerun the UI suite several times to confirm the failures are gone.
